where_extra_concentrates: Call/return frame machinery dominates the excess: pushStagedBytecodeExecFrame (12.63% self) + pushResolvedBytecodeClosure (11.44%) + tryPushSimpleResultMetamethod (10.05%) + opReturn simple_result fast path (vm.zig:15332, 7.48%) + FrameStack getPtr/shrinkTo/addOne lines (~8% combined) + syncFrame/defer/frame_identity (~4.5%) ~= 340 instr/iter equivalent, vs PUC's entire call path (luaD_precall 11.32% + luaT_callTMres 10.56% + luaD_call 7.19% + callbinTM 7.06% ~= 135 instr/iter). The frame push/pop machinery alone accounts for roughly +200 instr/iter of excess.

Per-instruction dispatch overhead inside runBytecodeDispatch: hooks_active_cached check (6.25%), stats.enabled check (2.58%), dispatch switch decode (7.07%), per-frame ctx.regs/ctx.boxed slice re-derivation (4.58%), cur_proto/cur_upvalues loads (~3.5%) — PUC pays none of these per instruction (no hooks flag check in the hot loop, no stats check, register window is a plain base pointer, no slice objects).

getTmByObj lookup itself is NOT the main excess: zig getTmByObj symbol (4.00%) + findBinaryTm line (1.53%) ~= 5.5% of zig samples ~= 37-51 instr/iter, vs PUC luaT_gettmbyobj (3.36%) + luaH_Hgetshortstr (2.10%) = 5.46% of PUC samples ~= 20 instr/iter. Excess is roughly +17-30 instr/iter, i.e. only ~3-5% of the +549 delta. The lookup is proportionally (and absolutely) only ~1.8-2.5x PUC — comparable to the overall 2.46x ratio, not a disproportionate hotspot.
metamethod_call_noalloc.getTmByObj_vs_luaT_gettmbyobj: zig lookup path (getTmByObj+findBinaryTm+inlined nodeLookupShortStrIdentity) ~= 5.5% of samples vs PUC (luaT_gettmbyobj+luaH_Hgetshortstr) 5.46% of samples; in absolute instr/iter ~37-51 vs ~20. Excess absolute cost exists (~2x) but is in line with the global 2.46x slowdown — the metamethod lookup is NOT where the disproportionate extra cost sits.

where_extra_concentrates: pushStagedBytecodeExecFrame alone is 15.42% self (~114 instr/iter) vs PUC luaD_precall 15.11% (~39 instr/iter) — the Lua-closure call setup costs ~3x more instructions in absolute terms.

Per-instruction overhead inside the dispatch loop: hooks check (9.08%) + stats check (4.95%) + pc advance (3.91%) + inst fetch (2.95%) + slice re-derivation (4.82%) + FrameStack getPtr lines (~7.4%) ~= 33% of samples ~= ~240 instr/iter, vs PUC's luaV_execute 84.22% (~217 instr/iter) which contains its equivalents nearly free (base-pointer register window, no per-instr hook/stats flags, direct ci pointer).
syncFrame (4.76% self + 1.76% defer line + frame_identity 1.73%) — PUC has no equivalent write-back; it keeps pc in the CallInfo directly.

conclusion.summary: For identical workloads luazig spends 2.5-2.9x the instructions of PUC. The excess is NOT in the metamethod/TM lookup itself (getTmByObj is proportionally no worse than the whole VM); it concentrates in (1) the staged frame push/pop machinery (pushStagedBytecodeExecFrame / pushResolvedBytecodeClosure / tryPushSimpleResultMetamethod / opReturn fast path / FrameStack getPtr-shrinkTo / syncFrame write-back), and (2) fixed per-instruction dispatch overhead (hooks_active_cached + stats.enabled checks, ctx.regs/ctx.boxed slice re-derivation per frame, activation_id load, defer syncFrame). PUC's equivalents (luaD_precall + direct ci->u.l.savedpc updates, plain base pointer) are dramatically cheaper in absolute instructions.
